summary: The study investigates the effect of rare earth cation size on the properties of REScO3 thin films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films were deposited using rare earth b-diketonate precursors (RE(thd)3) and ozone. The deposition temperature was 300 /C14 C, and the films showed varying crystallization behaviors depending on the RE3+ cation size. The results indicate that REScO3 films have potential as high-k gate dielectrics for MOSFETs.
evidence: A series of amorphous REScO3 films was deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using rare earth (RE) b-diketonate precursors RE(thd)3 together with ozone in an attempt to study the effect of the RE3+ cation size on various film properties. The deposition temperature was 300 /C14 C. REScO3 films were found to crystallize either as an orthorhombic perovskite phase or as a solid solution of the cubic C-type oxides. The results confirm that REScO3 films deposited by ALD are potential candidates for new generation high-k gate dielectrics.
